meta.label: Care homes
meta.attribution: These scores describe operators of care homes for older people in England, not individual homes. A home's own inspection report matters more than its operator's average, and the average moves as ratings are renewed. The inspection record is this catalogue's own count from the Care Quality Commission's published ratings file (as at 1 September 2026) joined to its care directory (23 September 2026). It covers homes the directory lists as residential or nursing homes for adults over 65 that hold an overall rating, grouped by provider name or, where the note says so, by the brand name CQC records. The score is the share rated Good or Outstanding among homes rated Outstanding, Good, Requires improvement or Inadequate, rounded. The file holds 10,546 such homes, and across the 10,479 that carry one of those four ratings the share is 81 per cent (440 Outstanding, 8,039 Good, 1,914 Requires improvement, 86 Inadequate). It is not a CQC statistic and CQC does not endorse it. Ratings are snapshots and many are old: between 14 and 95 per cent of an operator's ratings were published more than three years before the file date, and each note gives its figure. Choice is the count of an operator's homes divided by 2.5, capped at 95. It says nothing about vacancies, fees or whether a council will fund a place. Fees are not scored because operators set them home by home. Ownership is scored only where an operator's own statement or a regulator's published decision states it: 90 for a registered charity, 85 for a charitable housing association, 60 for a company that says it has no shareholders, and 20 where the competition regulator records that a US real estate investment trust owns the homes. Most operators carry no ownership score because their ownership could not be stated from a page read for this check. The competition regulator accepted undertakings over Welltower's purchase of the Barchester and HC-One property portfolios on 10 September 2026, and its case page was still open on 15 September 2026, so ownership at some homes is changing. Contains CQC data used under the Open Government Licence. Homes in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are regulated by other bodies and are not covered. This is not advice on choosing care. A council can carry out a needs assessment, and any home should be visited before a decision. Reviewed 2026-09. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Inspection record: share of the operator's older people's homes in England rated Good or Outstanding by CQC
Choice: how many homes it runs, so how easily a family can find one near them
Who it answers to: charity or no shareholders, against a property investor

products.name: Barchester Healthcare

safety.note: CQC's ratings file (as at 1 September 2026), joined to its care directory, lists 201 older people's care homes registered to Barchester Healthcare Homes Limited and Barchester Hellens Limited with an overall rating: 9 Outstanding, 169 Good, 21 Requires improvement and 2 Inadequate, which is 88.6 per cent Good or Outstanding, against 81 per cent across the 10,479 rated homes of this kind in England. 64 per cent of these ratings were published more than three years before the file date, and none carries an inherited rating.

accessibility.note: The CQC ratings file and care directory list 201 older people's care homes registered to Barchester Healthcare Homes Limited and Barchester Hellens Limited, 1.9 per cent of the 10,546 such homes in England. Scored as homes divided by 2.5, capped at 95; a bigger operator is likelier to have a home near a given family, but this says nothing about vacancies or fees.

ownership.note: The CMA's Phase 1 decision summary for case ME/7137/25 says Welltower Inc., which it describes as a US-based real estate investment trust, completed its acquisition on 23 and 24 October 2025 of the real estate interests in 275 care homes managed by Barchester Healthcare, and that operator-owned management companies now run the homes day to day. It also says that in the structure Welltower uses for some homes it can approve operators' annual business plans and operating budgets.

products.description: One of the largest operators in England, with most homes in the South East and South West. A US property investor bought the real estate of its homes in October 2025, and the competition regulator accepted remedies over local overlaps in September 2026.
